metadata.title: Material Plan Change: Stop Before the Scope Shifts
metadata.purpose: Answer one real question in the Plain register: when an agent's plan changes mid-task, the confirmation belongs before the change happens, not in a report after — only before can still change what happens. Lands the carry-out that a report after is an audit log and a question before is supervision.
metadata.anchor_pair: B01 -> B06 (the five-step plan card, step three flagged: planted with no split drawn, returns split into a before-path that pauses and asks and an after-path that finishes and only reports)

beats.narration_text: Someone assumes the fix is telling you after the agent changes its plan. But by then the change already happened. The real question: should it stop and tell you before it changes something?

shot.new_visual_element: Writer types 'My agent keeps adapting the plan on its own. When should it tell me after it changes something?', hesitates on 'after', corrects to 'before'

props.text:
My agent keeps adapting
the plan on its own.
When should it tell me
after it changes something?

beats.note: B00 is Remotion (BrutalistHesitantWriter) per hai-simple SKILL.md WRITER LAW. Single-word trigger ('after') swapped for a single-word replacement ('before') so buildActs()'s whitespace-token match fires (per the constitution/IVP redo lesson on multi-word triggers). TIMING LAW: narration + lead_silence_s 0.8 to give the typing a >=9s window; verify media/B00.mp4 >= 8s and that the correction ('after' -> 'before') is visible on a late frame.

beats.narration_text: Say you approve a five-step plan: pull last quarter's invoices, merge them into one report, and save it to the shared drive. Step three hits an invoice in a format the merge tool can't read. Adapting to that is normal — tool failures and missing formats are ordinary parts of how these agents work. The only question is whether the adaptation stays inside what you approved.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR - a five-step plan card, step three flagged with a format mismatch

production_viz.label: THE ANCHOR - five steps, step three flagged
production_viz.mechanic: THE ANCHOR. A numbered plan card listing five steps (pull invoices, merge, save to drive...) appears in full; step three gets a small terracotta flag marking a format mismatch, nothing else disturbed. THIS EXACT PLAN CARD RETURNS AT B06.

beats.narration_text: The natural guess sounds reasonable: let the agent keep going, and it can tell you afterward what it had to change to finish.

shot.new_visual_element: A TASK DONE gate, a completion report unrolling after it

production_viz.label: The natural guess - report afterward
production_viz.mechanic: A 'TASK DONE' gate on the left; a completion report card unrolling to its right, listing changes only after the gate has already passed.

beats.narration_text: But by the time you read that report, the library is already installed and the shared folder has already been read — changes you never named in the plan. The same three signs mark a change worth stopping for: a tool you didn't approve, data you didn't name, or a risk level higher than you agreed to.

shot.new_visual_element: The plan card gains two unnamed line items before the report appears; three trigger labels beside it

production_viz.label: The break - two unnamed changes already made
production_viz.mechanic: The B01 plan card reappears with two new line items silently added beneath it — 'installed library', 'read shared folder' — each flagged terracotta, sitting under a report card already stamped 'SENT'. Beside it, three labeled signs stack: 'DIFFERENT TOOL', 'NEW DATA', 'HIGHER RISK'.

beats.narration_text: Any one of those firing means stop before the next step, not after. A report written after the fact is an audit log. A question asked before the step is supervision — and only the question can still change what happens.

shot.new_visual_element: A timeline with two gate positions, BEFORE and AFTER; only BEFORE has a working stop

production_viz.label: Where the check sits decides what it can do
production_viz.mechanic: A horizontal timeline: a gate marked 'BEFORE' sits just ahead of the adaptation icon with a working stop sign that halts the arrow passing through; a gate marked 'AFTER' sits just past the same icon with a record-only icon, and the arrow has already passed through unstopped.

beats.narration_text: Stopping for everything would be its own problem. An agent that pauses on every small, in-scope adaptation — retrying a failed call, reading the one file it was told to read — is one nobody keeps approving.

shot.new_visual_element: A string of small in-scope adaptations, each interrupted by a stop sign, an approver waving them through unread

production_viz.label: Stopping for everything defeats itself
production_viz.mechanic: A row of small routine-adaptation icons (a retry arrow, a single-file read) each hitting its own stop sign in turn; an approver figure, worn down, stamps 'IGNORED' across the whole row without reading any of them.

beats.narration_text: Back to the invoice job: installing that library and reading that folder both clear the bar — a new tool, new data. The agent that stops there and asks returns control while the plan can still change. The agent that finishes and reports has already made the call for you.

shot.new_visual_element: THE ANCHOR RETURNS - the plan card splits into a before-path that pauses and an after-path that only reports

production_viz.label: The anchor returns - split into paused vs. only reported
production_viz.mechanic: THE B01 PLAN CARD RETURNS, identical, now split by a dividing line: on one side, a BEFORE path pauses at step three with a working stop icon, control visibly returned; on the other, an AFTER path shows step three already completed, a report card appearing beside it stamped 'DONE' — after the fact.

beats.narration_text: A change reported after it happens is an audit log. A change confirmed before it happens is supervision — and only supervision can still change what happens.

props.quote: A change reported after it happens is an audit log. A change confirmed before it happens is supervision — and only supervision can still change what happens.
props.sparkLine: Before is supervision. After is audit.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I want to build a material-plan-change detector into an agent workflow: a check that fires when the agent's actual plan diverges materially from what was authorized. Help me define what counts as a material change, what signal should trigger the check, and how to route the agent back to human approval when it fires. Liam, in for Bear.
